title: Ops playbook cards for batching & cache troubleshooting
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a compact, contextual "ops playbook" UI pattern in the Redwood Console to help platform and application engineers triage, explain, and remediate batching and KV-cache behavior without leaving the console. The playbook cards live on the per-route and per-model detail pages and surface quick diagnostics (hot prefixes, cache hit rate, batch sizes, latency variance), targeted explainers for why a recommendation was made, and one-click remediation paths (toggle cache tier, adjust batching window, open live trace). The goal is to reduce developer mean-time-to-resolution for common batching/cache regressions and enable non-expert users to apply safe changes with guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook cards available on route and model detail pages showing at least: cache hit rate, top 3 hot prefixes, median batch size, and latency P95.
Each card includes a 1-sentence rationale, a risk indicator (low/medium/high), and a recommended action with safe default parameters.
Prototype demonstrates an example remediation flow: open card -> preview change -> dry-run metrics simulation -> apply change via Console API -> show confirmation and rollback path.
Usability test with 6 platform engineers yields a task completion rate >= 80% for a typical cache-misconfiguration scenario and average time-to-resolution reduction compared to baseline flow.
Design handoff artifacts (Figma frames, tokens, interaction specs) delivered to ENG and linked in this ticket.
All copy reviewed by PM and security checklist (no secret leakage links) completed.
A design review with stakeholders scheduled and comments addressed.
tasks: Map common batching/cache failure patterns from ENG postmortems and support tickets
Design single-card variants for: diagnostics, recommendation, remediation preview, and follow-up actions
Create microcopy: rationale lines, risk levels, confirmation dialogs, and undo language
Prototype interaction in Figma with a simulated dry-run modal and sample telemetry widgets
Prepare QA checklist and acceptance flows for engineering handoff
Run 1 moderated usability session with internal SRE/Platform engineers
comments: [2025-11-04] Maya Chen: Kickoff notes — initial brief from PM (PM-4128) attached. Primary constraints: must not expose raw KV payloads in the UI; remediation actions limited to safe parameter ranges. Eng asked for a compact pattern that can be reused across other console cards.

[2025-11-05] Ravi Patel: First-pass sketches uploaded to Figma. Proposing 3 states for the playbook card: Normal, Alert (high-risk), and Muted (read-only for non-admins). Added placeholder for dry-run results table.
[2025-11-07] Product feedback (Ana Gomez): Recommend adding explicit cost delta estimate for each remediation suggestion (e.g., +0.8 tokens/req). This informs trade-offs for teams with tight budgets.

[2025-11-08] Eng sync (Oliver Park): ENG-2286 will provide the telemetry API endpoints for top prefixes and simulated dry-run. We need sample payloads by 2025-11-14. Blocking: dependency on ENG-2345 for endpoint auth headers.
[2025-11-10] Research plan (Maya): Recruiting 6 internal SREs for 30-min moderated sessions. Goal: observe mental model when diagnosing cache hit-rate drops and test card comprehension.

[2025-11-12] Design review scheduled: 2025-11-18 10:00 PT. Requested attendees: PM, 2 backend engs, 1 SRE, docs, and security. Action item: include a short accessibility checklist for color/risk labeling.

[2025-11-12] Decision: Use neutral language for recommendations ('Try increasing batching window to 30ms') and require an explicit 'Apply change' confirmation modal with intent acknowledgement. Undo path will call an API to revert settings and is surfaced for 10 minutes after change.
[2025-11-12] Link notes: Figma prototype and PRD attached in attachments. Prototype includes two sample scenarios: cold-cache startup and sudden latency spike caused by reduced batch sizes.
